page: Microsoft Azure D32s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz, providing 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyper-threading. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 4.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 262 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip compression, consistently fall into the weak category, representing the bottom 25% of tested hardware. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels in the middle 50%, as demonstrated by the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks, along with Passmark memory scores, also aligns with the middle 50% tier.

For specialized tasks, the D32s_v3 achieves average performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. Large language model inference speeds are average for small and medium models, but drop to poor for large models. This hardware profile offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose enterprise workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, and web serving. The tradeoff lies in its lower single-threaded efficiency, making it less optimal for single-core bound processes, while remaining cost-efficient for multi-threaded workloads that leverage its 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB of memory.
